correctness.rationale: For each element, unequal-labelled edges give disjoint invertible arrow-coordinate pivots, while the active equal-labelled edges give an oriented incidence matrix of graphic rank. Thus \(\operatorname{rank}(\operatorname{ad}_a)=|D|+r(S)\) in every characteristic, yielding the stated double edge-subset sum. For a forest, independent vertex differences imply \(q^c[1+(q^2-1)z]^m\). For a single cycle, transfer-matrix eigenvalues P_q and 1-z provide the provisional count, with exactly one full-cycle dependence class corrected. The package checker independently enumerates and row-reduces all 26,587 elements in twelve cases, including a multicyclic graph; finite tests are not substituted for proof.

originality.rationale: The closest primary full text (Can 2021, arXiv:2105.09826v1) proves torus-action complexity and orbit structure, not an element-centralizer dimension distribution over finite fields. Gargate and Gargate count polynomial-potent elements. Sokal provides the classical Potts/matroid expansion but no identification with incidence-algebra adjoint ranks. Published narrow Kronecker commutator results and a previously recorded general commutator-fiber assertion cover aggregate commuting statistics, not the claimed full elementwise rank polynomial, matroid invariance and toric/unicyclic closed laws. Searches found no equivalent stronger statement. Remaining priority risk is stated explicitly.

value.rationale: The invariant lists all centralizer dimensions and their multiplicities, not a single commuting probability. It gives complete finite-field answers on precisely the toric and height-two complexity-one poset families of an established structural classification, identifies the first-cycle correction, and demonstrates a family of nonisomorphic incidence algebras indistinguishable by the invariant for every field size. These conclusions explain a natural structural boundary and an invariant limitation, rather than an arbitrary finite tabulation.
